messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Shiny App: ImageMagick interface
parts:
Just to share, and hoping someone will be interested in enhancing it: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/ImageMagickCompression_single/

It uses the shinyAce package to render the ImageMagick command and to send it to the server. Actually you can upload any file and run any command, but the app intends to be a user-friendly interface for image compression (my camera generates huge jpeg files - that was my motivation to make this app).

The upload and the image rendering is slow on glimmer, it's better to run on your own computer: shiny::runGist("7186022")

I don't know what it doesn't work on Windows with the system() command. This problem is handled with this piece of code, and I don't know whether it is a universal solution:

    platform <- sessionInfo()$R.version$platform
    if(stringr::str_detect(platform, "linux")) system(comm) else shell(comm)

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Shiny App: ImageMagick interface
parts:
That is a risky application to put up, since you are essentially running the system command on arbitrary user code.

There is nothing that prevents a user from running passing rm -rf.

You should check with the Shiny team if this application is secure.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny App: ImageMagick interface
parts:
Now it is safe, the app should stop whenever "convert" is not the beginning of the command :

    if(!all(stringr::str_locate(comm, "convert") == c(1,7))) stopApp()

But there's an error somewhere in my code: the server always receives 'convert ...", even when the user types something else. So, accidentally, the app was already safe :)

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny App: ImageMagick interface
parts:
Stéphane,

Cool app! Unfortunately, as Ramnath pointed out, this is very vulnerable to a Code Injection attack. 

I'll email you privately with the details of the vulnerability, but for anyone else interested in developing such an app, we'd encourage any
app that accepts arbitrary R code or Shell scripts from the user to be distributed another way (such as the gist Stéphane provided)
to allow other to use the application, rather than being hosted on a public service like Glimmer or Spark.

Best,
Jeff
